label: Housing
assignment: Discover realistic ways a person without adequate housing in {service_area} could obtain safe temporary or permanent housing. Follow useful relationships rather than stopping at a directory listing: voucher providers to participating motels, organizations to specific programs, and temporary options to longer-term pathways. Investigate practical access and lived experience as well as official claims.
include: Emergency shelter and safe temporary lodging
Motel or hotel vouchers and the particular lodging providers that accept them
Transitional, supportive, sober, reentry, treatment-linked, and medically appropriate housing
Rent, deposit, utility, rapid-rehousing, subsidized, and permanent-housing pathways
Pet-friendly options and temporary animal care when pet rules block access
exclude: Ordinary market-rate real-estate listings without an affordability or access pathway
Housing directories that do not identify a currently reachable program or provider
Programs whose geography, population, or referral requirements exclude people in the service area
verificationQuestions: Can a person enter now, and what exact first step is required?
What eligibility, documentation, sobriety, family-composition, safety, or referral rules apply?
What costs, deposits, waitlists, time limits, transportation issues, and pet restrictions apply?
What longer-term path follows a temporary placement?

stages.title: Immediate safety and emergency access
stages.instruction: Investigate options that can help tonight or within days: emergency and seasonal shelter, domestic-violence and family or youth shelter, safe temporary lodging, motel vouchers, coordinated entry, crisis access, transportation, pet barriers, and the real intake path.

stages.title: Homelessness prevention and stabilization
stages.instruction: Investigate eviction prevention, rent and deposit help, utility help, diversion, rapid rehousing, flexible funds, case management, benefits, and practical pathways that can prevent or shorten homelessness.

stages.title: Transitional and specialized housing
stages.instruction: Investigate transitional, supportive, recovery, reentry, treatment-linked, medically appropriate, veteran, family, youth, disability, and other population-specific housing that realistically serves the area.

stages.title: Permanent pathways and gap review
stages.instruction: Investigate affordable and subsidized housing, housing authorities, waitlists, permanent supportive housing, landlord or rental pathways, and important gaps. Cross-check earlier findings and pursue missing relationships or access details needed for a useful review.
